title: Motorways: Lanes & Rules for Lorries
whatItIs: Lorries over 7.5 tonnes must not use the right-hand lane of a motorway with three or more lanes. Keep left unless overtaking, and remember your lower speed limit.

keyFacts.text: Goods vehicles over 7.5 t MUST NOT use the right-hand lane of a motorway with three or more lanes.
Also MUST NOT use it: 3.5 to 7.5 t goods vehicles required to have a speed limiter, and any vehicle towing a trailer.
Goods vehicles over 7.5 t MUST NOT exceed 60 mph on a motorway.

keyFacts: Many large vehicles have speed limiters that restrict them to 56 mph (90 km/h), even on a motorway.
Keep in the left lane unless overtaking. Overtake only on the right, and don't cut in on the vehicle you've passed.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT stop on the carriageway or hard shoulder except in an emergency, or when told to.

visual.caption: Which lanes a goods vehicle over 7.5 tonnes may use

rows: Both lanes (the right-hand lane only to overtake)
Every lane except the right-hand lane
notes: The same lane ban applies to any vehicle towing a trailer, and to 3.5 to 7.5 t goods vehicles that must have a speed limiter.

a.label: Speed limit for lorries over 7.5 t
points: Set by law: you MUST NOT exceed it

b.label: Speed limiter
points: Many large vehicles are restricted to 56 mph
A device on the vehicle, not the legal limit

onTheTest.question: You're driving a 40-tonne articulated lorry on a three-lane motorway. Which lanes may you use?
options: The left and middle lanes only
The middle and right-hand lanes only
onTheTest.why: Goods vehicles over 7.5 tonnes must not use the right-hand lane of a motorway with three or more lanes (except in prescribed circumstances).

onTheTest.question: What's the national speed limit on a motorway for a goods vehicle over 7.5 tonnes?
onTheTest.why: The motorway limit for goods vehicles over 7.5 tonnes is 60 mph. 56 mph is the speed many speed limiters are set to, not the legal limit.

traps: 56 mph is a speed limiter setting, not the speed limit: it's 60 mph on a motorway for lorries over 7.5 t.
The right-hand lane ban is for motorways with three or more lanes, not two-lane motorways.
Missed your exit? Carry on to the next one: you MUST NOT reverse, cross the central reservation or drive against the flow.
Don't move to a lane on your left to overtake.

sources.ref: Motorway signs, signals and road markings (page 91)

jurisdictionNotes.text: Goods vehicles over 7.5 t in Scotland: 60 mph on motorways, but 50 mph on dual carriageways and 40 mph on single carriageways.
